scope: 39 locally relevant families listed in the Google Sheet Family Study Index

status_definitions.joey_sufficient: Joey archive contains enough morphology/ecology media to build a strong first-pass family lesson; authoritative sources still verify terminology and exceptions.
status_definitions.joey_plus_authoritative_backfill: Joey material is useful and should be retained, but one or more essential diagnostic structures or local-lineage examples are missing.
status_definitions.authoritative_backfill_required: Joey archive is too sparse for a responsible family lesson; build the family module primarily from authoritative botanical sources and use Joey only as supplemental context if available.

rubric: At least one reliable 'where to look first' diagnostic cue.
Reproductive morphology represented or clearly sourceable.
Vegetative morphology represented where diagnostically useful.
Local or structurally comparable examples sufficient to avoid overfitting to one unusual taxon.
Likely confusing local families identified for side-by-side teaching.
Traits are structural/measurable rather than flower color or vague gestalt.

families.where_to_look_first: Inflorescence architecture first; then spikelets, glumes, lemma/palea, awns, ligule, collar and sheath.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Joey gives a useful branching-vs-compact inflorescence comparison and a graminoid video set, but not enough exact ligule/collar/sheath/spikelet macro coverage.
families.backfill_action: Backfill exact local macro images of ligule, collar, sheath, node, spikelet, glumes, lemma/palea and awns; build a grass-vs-sedge-vs-rush comparison.
backfill_progress: three generic open-license spikelet teaching-image candidates locked
priority cards complete for Andropogon gerardii, Aristida purpurea, Eragrostis intermedia, Muhlenbergia lindheimeri and Panicum virgatum
five species-specific public-reuse images locked plus study-only collar/spikelet references
local/public-reuse collar macro coverage remains incomplete for some species
remaining five priority queue items resolved: Nassella leucotricha, Sorghastrum nutans, Sporobolus compositus, Tripsacum dactyloides plus Bothriochloa taxonomy correction
all ten original priority-1 backfill queue items resolved: 9 training cards + 1 taxonomy resolution

families.where_to_look_first: Start at the node: opposite leaves + usually square stem, then inspect the bilabiate flower and 4-lobed ovary/nutlets.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Excellent Salvia sets plus Scutellaria, Dicerandra, Trichostema and Ocimum cover habit, nodes, calyx, corolla and reproductive structures.
families.backfill_action: Use authoritative sources only to verify the family summary and local exceptions.

families.where_to_look_first: Opposite leaves and clustered/spicate flowers; confirm corolla, calyx and fruit rather than relying on square stems.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Lantana, Verbena and Lippia material gives habit, leaf arrangement, flowers and ecology.
families.backfill_action: Backfill one clean fruit example and verify distinctions from Lamiaceae.

families.where_to_look_first: Ask whether the 'flower' is actually a head: find the involucre/phyllaries, ray florets, disk/tubular florets and pappus.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Extremely strong: multiple heads, phyllaries, dissected capitula, ray/disk florets, styles, pappus and syncephaly examples.
families.backfill_action: Verify terminology and local tribal exceptions; otherwise Joey coverage is excellent.

families.where_to_look_first: Look for an inferior ovary below a usually 4-merous flower; then inspect stigma shape, floral tube and capsule.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Oenothera plus Clarkia/Chamerion references give useful flower and pollination context but not a complete family character set.
families.backfill_action: Backfill inferior ovary, epigynous flower, stigma, capsule and seed images from local Oenothera/Gaura-lineage taxa.

families.where_to_look_first: Opposite leaves first; then confirm small 4-merous flowers with only 2 stamens and the family-specific fruit type.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Only a very small Joey image footprint.
families.backfill_action: Build from local Fraxinus/Forestiera with flower, fruit, bud and opposite-leaf examples.

families.where_to_look_first: Find the fruit: a legume is the strongest clue. Then determine papilionoid vs mimosoid/caesalpinioid flower architecture and inspect compound leaves.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Outstanding flower and fruit diversity: Tephrosia, Indigofera, Lupinus, Dalea, Mimosa, Senna, Aeschynomene, Inga and others.
families.backfill_action: Authoritative verification only; add local genus-specific exceptions later.

families.where_to_look_first: Woody habit + alternate leaves; inspect resinous/aromatic tissues, small flowers and drupes, then compare leaf architecture.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Useful Joey video/external material but too little exact macro morphology.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local Rhus/Toxicodendron flower, drupe, rachis/leaflet and twig/bud characters.

families.where_to_look_first: Look at the flower center: numerous stamens, often forming a staminal column; also check stellate hairs, epicalyx/calyx and fruit.
likely_confusions: Sterculioid Malvaceae can look unlike Hibiscus
families.joey_coverage_summary: Excellent staminal-column, nectary, calyx, fruit, pubescence, Hermannia, Corchorus and Ayenia material.
families.backfill_action: Verify subfamily variation so the learner does not overfit to a Hibiscus-type flower.

families.where_to_look_first: Go to the reproductive center: usually many free stamens and multiple free pistils/achenes; floral parts are often separate rather than fused.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Only a probable Clematis drummondii field mention plus limited video context.
families.backfill_action: Build a local Clematis-centered set: opposite leaves/vining habit, petaloid sepals, many stamens, aggregate achenes with plumose styles; add one non-Clematis local genus for family breadth.

families.where_to_look_first: Inspect foliage type and cones: scale/awl-like leaves, opposite/whorled arrangement, small woody/fleshy cones; Taxodium is a notable local exception.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Taxodium and Hesperocyparis give useful trunk, habitat and cone imagery.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local Juniperus scale leaves, berry-like cones, male cones and twig arrangement; explicitly contrast Taxodium.

families.where_to_look_first: Check for milky latex and fused corolla; in milkweeds/milkvines go straight to corona, gynostegium, pollinia and paired follicles.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Excellent Asclepias, Matelea/Gonolobinae and other Apocynaceae morphology, including follicles and seeds.
families.backfill_action: Authoritative verification plus a non-Asclepiadoid local example if available.

families.where_to_look_first: Find an areole. Then read ribs/tubercles, spines, flower position and fruit.
families.joey_coverage_summary: One of the strongest Joey families: areoles, ribs, tubercles, spines, multiple growth forms, flowers, fruits and stress anatomy.
families.backfill_action: No major backfill needed beyond local-species representation.

families.where_to_look_first: For local Agave/Yucca/Hesperaloe, start with rosette architecture and leaf armature, then inspect the 3+3 perianth and ovary/fruit.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Strong Agave/Yucca/Hesperaloe morphology, rosettes, teeth, terminal spines, inflorescences and flowers.
families.backfill_action: Clarify current APG subfamilies and local genus distinctions.

families.where_to_look_first: For hackberries, start with the strongly 3-veined leaf base, often asymmetric base, then inspect drupes and twig/bud characters.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No meaningful Joey family coverage.
families.backfill_action: Build Celtis-focused local package: leaf venation, asymmetry, drupes, hackberry nipple galls as ecology context, twig/bud and bark; compare Ulmus.

families.where_to_look_first: On local Passiflora, find axillary tendrils and the elaborate flower: corona filaments, androgynophore and 3 stigmas.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No meaningful Joey coverage.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local Passiflora habit, tendril origin, corona, anthers/stigmas, fruit and leaf variation.

families.where_to_look_first: Inspect fruit and leaf arrangement: samaras in Acer, inflated capsules in some genera, or soapberry drupes; flowers are usually small.
families.joey_coverage_summary: One exact Acer image plus limited video context.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local Acer/Sapindus/Ungnadia examples: opposite vs alternate leaves, samara/capsule/drupaceous fruit, flowers and buds.

families.where_to_look_first: For local Penstemon-type plants, inspect the bilabiate/tubular corolla, 4 fertile stamens plus staminode when present, and capsule.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Only external beardtongue media references.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local Penstemon flower side/front, staminode, stamens, calyx, capsule and opposite leaves.

families.where_to_look_first: Woody plant with alternate simple leaves; inspect tiny 4-merous flowers and berry-like drupes, noting dioecy where relevant.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Excellent Ilex flower close-up but only one family example.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local Ilex fruit, leaf margin/venation, twig/bud and male-vs-female flowers.

families.where_to_look_first: Opposite leaves plus a large tubular/bilabiate flower; confirm elongated capsule and often winged seeds.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No meaningful Joey coverage.
families.backfill_action: Build Chilopsis/Catalpa/Campsis local comparison with flower, capsule, seeds, leaf arrangement and bud/twig.

families.where_to_look_first: Find the fruit/cupule: acorns are decisive. Then inspect bud clusters, leaf margins, bark and cup scales.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Strong Quercus material including Hinckley oak plus video coverage of oak morphology/ecology.
families.backfill_action: Backfill only local oak species comparisons and bud/cupule detail as needed.

families.where_to_look_first: Opposite leaves and bilateral flowers; the big confirmation is a capsule with retinacula/jaculators that explosively eject seeds.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Joey gives an excellent explosive-dehiscence concept but almost no exact local family morphology.
families.backfill_action: Backfill Ruellia/Dyschoriste flower, capsule, retinacula, seed and leaf/node macro images.

families.where_to_look_first: Look for fleshy/sheathing leaves and 3-petaled flowers, often with strongly differentiated fertile stamens and staminodes.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No Joey coverage.
families.backfill_action: Backfill Tradescantia/Commelina flower, sheath, node, stamens/staminodes and capsule.

families.where_to_look_first: Rough alternate leaves with asymmetric bases and strong pinnate veins; confirm samara fruit in Ulmus.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No Joey coverage.
families.backfill_action: Build Ulmus package: leaf asymmetry, serration, samaras, buds and bark; side-by-side with Celtis.

families.where_to_look_first: Vine habit with tendrils opposite the leaves, swollen nodes and berry clusters.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No Joey coverage.
families.backfill_action: Backfill Vitis/Parthenocissus/Cissus habit, tendril position, node, flower cluster, berry and leaf variation.

families.where_to_look_first: Inspect flower merosity and anthers: typically 6 tepals + 6 stamens, with anthers opening by valves; fruit often a berry.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Only light video context.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local Mahonia/Berberis/Nandina-if-relevant comparison using native taxa only for canonical local lesson; flower, anther valves, berry and leaf architecture.

families.where_to_look_first: Pinnately compound leaves + husked nut; inspect male catkins, female flowers, pith and twig scars.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Only external/transcript Juglans microcarpa context.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local Juglans/Carya leaves, catkins, husks/nuts, buds, pith and bark.

families.where_to_look_first: First ask whether it is parasitic/hemiparasitic; then inspect bilateral flowers, bracts and capsule. Fully parasitic genera may lack chlorophyll.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Excellent Aphyllon/Esterhazya material demonstrates parasitic and floral morphology.
families.backfill_action: Backfill a local green hemiparasite such as Castilleja/Buchnera to prevent overfitting to achlorophyllous parasites.

families.where_to_look_first: Look for compound umbels, sheathing leaf bases and a 2-part schizocarp; stems are often hollow/furrowed.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No Joey coverage.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local Apiaceae with umbel, involucre/involucel, leaf sheath, flower and schizocarp.

families.where_to_look_first: Go straight to the bizarre perianth: pipe/trap-like fused tube, inferior ovary and no typical petal whorl.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Excellent Aristolochia erecta flower and host-interaction images.
families.backfill_action: Authoritative verification only; add fruit/seed if missing.

families.where_to_look_first: Alternate simple entire leaves + persistent calyx on a berry; flowers often unisexual.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Only video context.
families.backfill_action: Backfill Diospyros texana/virginiana bark, leaves, male/female flowers, persistent calyx and fruit.

families.where_to_look_first: Ignore flowers—inspect frond division and especially sori position; many Pteridaceae have marginal/submarginal sori with false indusia.
families.joey_coverage_summary: One excellent fertile-frond image but not enough local breadth.
families.backfill_action: Backfill local cheilanthoid fern fronds, sori/false indusia, scales/hairs and drought-curling habit.

families.where_to_look_first: Palmately lobed leaves + exfoliating mottled bark + hanging spherical flower/fruit heads.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No Joey coverage.
families.backfill_action: Build Platanus occidentalis local module with bark, leaf, stipule, spherical heads and achenes.

families.where_to_look_first: Opposite/whorled leaves are not enough—find the interpetiolar stipules. Flowers often have an inferior ovary.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Bouvardia gives excellent long-tubed flower morphology plus supporting media.
families.backfill_action: Backfill a local Rubiaceae showing interpetiolar stipules, ovary position and fruit.

families.where_to_look_first: Scratch for milky latex; inspect alternate entire leaves, small flowers and fleshy fruit with large glossy seeds.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Only Joey thornscrub text context for Sideroxylon.
families.backfill_action: Backfill Sideroxylon celastrinum flower, fruit/seed, latex, thorn/twig and leaf architecture.

families.where_to_look_first: Look for colored/white latex, 2 sepals that often fall early, 4 petals, many stamens and a capsule.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No Joey coverage.
families.backfill_action: Backfill Argemone local examples: prickly foliage, latex, sepals, crumpled petals, stamens, stigma/capsule and seeds.

families.where_to_look_first: Look for stipules and a hypanthium; then determine fruit type—drupe, pome, aggregate fruit, etc.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Good Prunus texana/mexicana-style fruit/seed/bark material and Polylepis/other external examples.
families.backfill_action: Backfill family-wide hypanthium/stipule/fruit diversity so the learner does not equate Rosaceae with Prunus only.

families.where_to_look_first: Twining/trailing habit + alternate leaves; confirm a 5-fold funnel-shaped, plicate corolla and capsule, often with milky sap.
families.joey_coverage_summary: No meaningful Joey family coverage despite high local relevance.
families.backfill_action: Backfill Ipomoea leaf attachment, sepals, corolla folds, stamens/style, capsule/seeds and side-by-side local species comparisons.

families.where_to_look_first: Woody shrub/tree; inspect urceolate or otherwise sympetalous flowers, specialized anthers and often evergreen/leathery leaves.
families.joey_coverage_summary: Strong Arbutus, Lyonia, Pyrola and other Ericaceae media, including bark, fruit, twig and unusual mycoheterotrophic form.
families.backfill_action: Authoritative verification only; tailor examples to the two local taxa.
